How much commission did each stylist earn?

Choose the period and the commission rates used for services and retail. Gather each stylist’s eligible sales net of discounts, refunds and taxes and enter any tips separately. Use the same spelling of each team member’s name on all their rows. Compare the totals with your point-of-sale report before sending out statements.

Manage salon bookings on Shopify →

Worked example

A stylist records $800 in service sales, $150 in product sales and $60 in tips. A 40% service rate gives $320 and a 10% retail rate gives $15. Adding the $60 tips gives $395 for the period.

Salon Commission Calculator FAQ

Are service and product sales paid at the same rate?

You can enter separate percentages. For example, set a service rate of 40% and a retail rate of 10%, or use zero for a category that earns no commission.

Can I paste more than one sale for the same stylist?

Yes. Rows with the same team member name are grouped together. Check for spelling or spacing differences when preparing sales from more than one source.

How are tips handled?

Enter the tip amount allocated to that stylist. It appears separately and is added in full to the calculated commissions. If your salon pools tips, allocate the individual amounts before entering them.

What if individual stylists have different commission rates?

The entered rates apply to everyone in one run. Group people with the same rates together, or calculate separate statements for each rate arrangement.

Do I enter gross receipts or net sales?

Use eligible service and retail sales after discounts, refunds and taxes. Keep the tips in their own column so they do not also earn a sales commission.

Is this a payroll statement?

It is a breakdown of the sales commissions and tips you enter. Base pay, hours, deductions and payroll taxes belong in your payroll system.
